newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian premier leaves for U.S., Italy.
newsitem.headline: Albanian premier leaves for U.S., Italy.

text.p: Albania's interim Prime Minister Bashkim Fino left for a five-day official visit to the United States on Saturday, saying he would seek Washington's assistance in holding early elections.
Fino was to stop off in Italy and hold talks with Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini on his way to the United States.
He left just a day after European envoy Franz Vranitzky secured an agreement from Albania's 10 main political parties to break an impasse in holding early elections in June.

"We express our belief that, alongside the other nations and organisations involved, the United States will give its assistance through its well-known expertise throughout the election process," Fino said in a statement issued on his departure.
"There is no doubt this will have positive consequences for the credibility and transparency of the elections."
Fino heads a nine-party government of National Reconciliation set up in March to halt Albania's drift to anarchy as anger over the collapse of pyramid investment schemes erupted in widespread riots.

"The messages and concrete actions of the United States have had an essential influence for calming down the situation, the return to democratic normality and the re-birth of hope to start the political, economic, moral and institutional restoration of our country," the Albanian prime minister said.
Early elections were agreed between Albania's main parties as part of the deal setting up the National Reconciliation Government.

But disagreements between President Sali Berisha's Democratic Party and the rest over how many of the seats should be decided by proportional representation were threatening to scupper the vote until Vranitzky intervened.
Party representatives are hammering out a new compromise electoral law over the weekend which will be adopted by the government on Monday.

If the election is to be held on June 29 as anticipated, the Democrat-dominated parliament has until Thursday, May 15 to approve the new law to allow President Berisha to issue his decree the requisite 45 days before the vote.
In the U.S. Fino will meet U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright on Monday. He will leave on Wednesday.

Fino, who travelled to the U.S. with Albanian Finance Minister Arben Malaj, said he would also meet congressmen and senators, senior politicians and businessmen as well as heads of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank.
